cues.zh: 我们的食物营养是不是越来越少了？
cues.en: Is our food becoming less nutritious?

cues.zh: 很多人都说，几十年来，我们食物中的营养含量一直在下降。
cues.en: Many people claim that the nutrient content in our food has been decreasing over the decades.

cues.zh: 但这是真的吗？我们需要担心吗？
cues.en: But is this really true, and should we be worried?

cues.zh: 一项发表于2004年的研究调查了43种常见的园艺作物，
cues.en: A study published in 2004 looked at 43 different common garden crops,

cues.zh: 分析它们的营养价值在1950年至1999年间发生了怎样的变化。
cues.en: and how their nutritional value had changed between 1950 and 1999.

cues.zh: 研究发现，这些植物的蛋白质含量平均下降了约6%，
cues.en: Now, what they found was that on average, the protein content of those plants decreased by about 6%,

cues.zh: 维生素C下降了15%，维生素B2更是大幅下降了38%。
cues.en: Vitamin C decreased 15%, and vitamin B2 by a whopping 38 percent.

cues.zh: 研究人员还发现，铁和钙等矿物质的含量也有所下降。
cues.en: They also noticed declines and minerals like iron and calcium.

cues.zh: 不过，这些数据仍有争议，因为你想想，
cues.en: Now, there is some debate around the numbers because, well,

cues.zh: 1950年时，我们到底能多准确地测量这些营养成分？
cues.en: How well could we really have measured those nutrients back in 1950?

cues.zh: 但人们还是担心，我们今天吃的食物，营养可能不如50年前的同类蔬菜。
cues.en: But there is still this concern that the food we're eating today might be less nutritious than, say, the same vegetables 50 years ago.

cues.zh: 最近的其他几项研究也表明，某种趋势正在显现。
cues.en: Several other recent studies also suggest a pattern is emerging.

cues.zh: 那么，如果我们正在目睹一场营养崩塌，原因到底是什么？
cues.en: So if we're witnessing a nutrient collapse, what's causing it?

cues.zh: 很多人指出的一个因素，是土壤肥力的流失。
cues.en: One factor that many people point to is depletion of the soils.

cues.zh: 鉴于植物是从土壤中汲取养分，
cues.en: Given plants to draw their nutrients up from the soil,

cues.zh: 人们曾认为集约化农业是导致养分枯竭的元凶。
cues.en: intense farming practices were thought to be the cause of nutrient depletion.

cues.zh: 如果看微量营养素，比如矿物质，植物体内的含量确实在下降。
cues.en: If you look at micronutrients, things like minerals, well, there are decreasing levels in plants.

cues.zh: 但是，农民一直以来都在竭力维护土壤，
cues.en: But, farmers have always put a lot of effort into maintaining their soils,

cues.zh: 并使用肥料来确保植物获得所需的全部养分，
cues.en: and using fertilizers to ensure that the plants have all the nutrients they need,

cues.zh: 这就让那个说法显得没那么有说服力了。
cues.en: which makes that argument less convincing.

cues.zh: 我们种出来的作物个头依然很大，如果土壤里没有必需的养分，它们根本不可能长得这么好。
cues.en: We're still getting big plants, and they wouldn't grow that well if they didn't have the nutrients they need in the soil.

cues.zh: 那么，营养素含量还可能因为什么而下降呢？
cues.en: So why else might nutrients be declining?

cues.zh: 一种可能是选择性育种。
cues.en: One possibility is that it's selective breeding.

cues.zh: 如果你看看今天的玉米等作物，把它们和祖先相比，几乎认不出来了，
cues.en: If you look at crops like corn today, they're barely recognizable when you compare them to their ancestors,

cues.zh: 也就是这些作物最初被培育出来的野生玉米。
cues.en: the wild corn from which these were bred.

cues.zh: 基本上，自从农业出现以来，
cues.en: Basically since the advent of agriculture,

cues.zh: 我们一直在培育粮食作物，以提高产量、抵抗病虫害和适应气候变化。
cues.en: we have been breeding our food crops for higher yields, for resistance to pests and changes in the climate.

cues.zh: 总的来说，我们成功了。作物比以往任何时候都更大、生长更快。
cues.en: And, by and large, we've been successful. Crops are now bigger and grow faster than ever before.

cues.zh: 但它们更有营养吗？
cues.en: But are they more nutritious?

cues.zh: 也许在追求其他目标的过程中，我们不知不觉地把营养从食物中培育掉了。
cues.en: Maybe we've accidentally been breeding the nutrition out of our foods in pursuit of other objectives.

cues.zh: 很难真正评估选择性育种到底有多大影响，
cues.en: It's tough to really assess how big of a factor selective breeding is,

cues.zh: 因为我们不容易把现在的农产品和一百年前或一千年前的同类农产品进行比较。
cues.en: because we can't easily compare this produce to the same produce a hundred years ago or a thousand years ago.

cues.zh: 所以我们需要别的办法来判断，究竟是选择性育种导致了这种减少，还是另有原因。
cues.en: So we need something else to be able to determine whether it's selective breeding causing this decrease or something else.

cues.zh: 真正有用的是那种从未经过选择性育种的植物。
cues.en: What would be really helpful would be a plant that has never been selectively bred.

cues.zh: 上哪儿找这样的植物呢？这时候杂草就派上用场了。
cues.en: Where would you find one like that? Well, this is where weeds come in handy.

cues.zh: 在北美，有一种野花叫一枝黄花。
cues.en: In North America, there is a wild flower called goldenrod.

cues.zh: 它是蜜蜂重要的蛋白质来源，但对人类来说不是。
cues.en: It's an important source of protein for bees, but not humans.

cues.zh: 因此它一直保持野生状态，或者说未被选择性育种触碰过，但你怎么知道100年或200年前的一枝黄花是什么样呢？
cues.en: And so, it has remained wild, or untouched by selective breeding, but how would you know what goldenrod was like 100 or 200 years ago?

cues.zh: 史密森学会一直保存着数百份一枝黄花样本，最早可追溯到1842年。
cues.en: The Smithsonian Institute have been keeping hundreds of samples of goldenrod dating all the way back to 1842.

cues.zh: 利用这些样本以及他们在2014年采集的样本，
cues.en: Using these samples and samples they collected in 2014,

cues.zh: 科学家们得以将现代一枝黄花与一百多年前的一枝黄花进行比较，结果令人震惊。
cues.en: scientists were able to compare modern goldenrod with goldenrod from over a hundred years ago, and the results were astounding.

cues.zh: 他们发现，在这段时期内，一枝黄花花粉中的蛋白质含量下降了 30%。
cues.en: They found that there was a 30% decrease in the amount of protein in the goldenrod pollen over that period.

cues.zh: 如果不是人工选择性育种的原因，
cues.en: If it's not selective breeding,

cues.zh: 那还有什么导致了一枝黄花在过去约 150 年里变得越来越没营养？
cues.en: what else has contributed to goldenrod becoming less nutritious over the last 150 years or so?

cues.zh: 一个相当令人惊讶的观点是，二氧化碳可能在其中起到了关键作用。
cues.en: One rather surprising idea was that carbon dioxide could play a vital role.

cues.zh: [历史影像]：这里我们可以看到横截面，空气带着二氧化碳气体微粒进入植物，并渗透到每个活细胞中。
cues.en: [Old time video]: Here we see in cross-section air with its particles of carbon dioxide gas enters the plant and makes its way into every living cell.

cues.zh: CO2 就像空气中植物的养料，它基本上能促进所有植物的生长。
cues.en: CO2 is like plant food in the air. It basically increases the growth of all plants.

cues.zh: 在过去的几个世纪里，大气中的 CO2 浓度大幅增加，
cues.en: Over the last couple of centuries, the level of CO2 in the atmosphere has increased a lot,

cues.zh: 从大约 280 ppm 增加到了如今的 400 多 ppm。
cues.en: from about 280 parts per million to over 400 parts per million today.

cues.zh: 听起来可能不算多，
cues.en: Now, that might not sound like a lot,

cues.zh: 但如果把它看作植物养料，这可是增加了将近 50%，
cues.en: but if you're thinking of it as plant food, we're talking about an increase by almost 50%,

cues.zh: 而且从太空中就能看到这种影响。
cues.en: and we can see the impact from space.

cues.zh: 这被称为地球变绿现象。
cues.en: It's called the greening of the planet.

cues.zh: 科学家通过名为 FACE 的实验追踪二氧化碳对植物的影响，
cues.en: Scientists have been tracking the impact of CO2 on plants via experiments called FACE,

cues.zh: FACE 是“自由空气二氧化碳浓度升高”的缩写。
cues.en: which stands for Free Air Carbon dioxide Enrichment.

cues.zh: 他们在农作物生长的区域注入更多二氧化碳来开展实验，
cues.en: Their experiments run by injecting more CO2 into the area where plant crops are grown,

cues.zh: 结果发现，大气中的二氧化碳越多，小麦、大麦、水稻和土豆就长得越快。
cues.en: and they find that wheat, barley, rice and potatoes; they will grow faster if there's more CO2 in the atmosphere.

cues.zh: 但问题是，它们的营养价值未必会提高，只是碳水化合物含量增加了。
cues.en: But here's the thing. They don't necessarily become more nutritious, they simply put on more carbs.

cues.zh: 在日本和中国开展的其他研究中，
cues.en: In other studies conducted in Japan and China,

cues.zh: 科学家向水稻田注入二氧化碳，模拟预计 50 年后会出现的二氧化碳浓度。
cues.en: scientists pumped carbon dioxide into rice crops to simulate the kind of CO2 concentrations expected in 50 years time.

cues.zh: 平均而言，蛋白质含量下降了 10%，铁含量下降了 8%，锌含量下降了 5%，
cues.en: On average, protein levels fell by 10 percent iron by 8 percent and zinc by 5 percent,

cues.zh: 但营养物质浓度降低，并不一定意味着植物所含营养物质的总量也减少了。
cues.en: But a lower concentration of nutrients doesn't necessarily correlate with a decline in the plant's nutrient contents.

cues.zh: 这叫做稀释效应。
cues.en: It's called the dilution effect.

cues.zh: 那么这一切对我们意味着什么？
cues.en: So what does all this mean for us?

cues.zh: 科学家估计，到2050年，发展中国家多达1.5亿人
cues.en: Well, by 2050 scientists estimate that up to a hundred and fifty million people in the developing world

cues.zh: 可能面临蛋白质缺乏的边缘，因为他们主食中的蛋白质含量在下降。
cues.en: may be on the verge of protein deficiency, due to the decreasing levels of protein in their staple foods.

cues.zh: 那么这是否意味着我们都应该服用维生素和补充剂？
cues.en: So does that mean we should all be taking vitamins and supplements?

cues.zh: 嗯，不。至少现在还不必。
cues.en: Well, no. At least, not yet.

cues.zh: 因为营养素的下降幅度足够小，你仍然可以通过均衡饮食获取所需的一切，
cues.en: Because the nutrient declines are small enough that you should still be able to get everything you need from a well balanced diet,

cues.zh: 包括大量水果和蔬菜。
cues.en: Including plenty of fruits and veggies.

cues.zh: 但是，不断上升的二氧化碳水平和稀释效应可能正在加剧肥胖症的流行。
cues.en: But, the increasing levels of CO2 and the dilution effect may be exacerbating the obesity epidemic.

cues.zh: 思路是这样的：
cues.en: The thinking goes like this:

cues.zh: 当我们摄入一定量的蛋白质时，我们会感到饱足。
cues.en: We feel full, or satiated, when we've consumed a certain amount of protein.

cues.zh: 所以，如果蛋白质含量下降了
cues.en: So if the protein levels are going down

cues.zh: 我们可能就得摄入更多食物、更多碳水和更多脂肪，才能获得同等水平的蛋白质。
cues.en: We may have to eat more food, more carbohydrates, and more fats to achieve the same level of protein.

cues.zh: 这可能会让我们变得更胖。
cues.en: And that may make us fatter.

cues.zh: 虽然这仍是一个有争议的理论，但越来越明确的是，大气环境的改变，
cues.en: While this is still a contentious theory what is becoming increasingly clear is that the changing atmosphere,

cues.zh: 特别是二氧化碳浓度的上升，正在改变我们所吃的食物。
cues.en: specifically the rising level of CO2, is changing the food we eat.

cues.zh: 嘿，希望你喜欢这个视频。
cues.en: Hey, I hope you enjoyed that.

cues.zh: 我做这个视频，算是我的新长篇纪录片《Vitamania》的衍生配套内容，
cues.en: I made this video as kind of a companion piece to my new feature-length documentary called Vitamania,

cues.zh: 内容全都是关于维生素和补充剂的科学真相与种种乱象。
cues.en: all about the sense and nonsense of vitamins and supplements.

cues.zh: 如果你还没看的话，可以直接点击这里观看这部纪录片。
cues.en: You can watch that documentary if you haven't already by clicking right here.

cues.zh: 全球都可以观看，除了法国和德国，因为该片将于 9 月 25 日在当地电视上播出。对此我深表遗憾，
cues.en: It's available globally, except for France and Germany because it'll be on your TV on September 25th. I'm really sorry about that,

cues.zh: 但我真的非常感谢大家，是你们让我既能做 YouTube 视频，又能制作大型国际电视纪录片。
cues.en: but I really appreciate you making it possible for me to make both YouTube videos and Big international TV documentaries.

cues.zh: 这一路很有意思，真的，没有你我做不到。
cues.en: It's been a lot of fun and really, I couldn't have done it without you.
